subject: Network segmentation evaluation & air-gapped deployment options (next steps)
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Alan Walker <alan.walker@medgest.com>; Katie Lin <katie@medgest.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-07-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Network segmentation evaluation & air-gapped deployment options (next steps)

Hi Alan / Katie —

Thanks again for the call earlier — great to learn more about the MedGest POC goals and the regulatory constraints on device telemetry and PHI handling. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment: 

High-level security posture you described:
- MedGest requires data residency in the us-east-1 region, all PHI to remain within private subnets, and strict egress controls.
- SOC 2 Type II: in progress; SOC 2 readiness assessment completed (expected attestation Q4 2028).
- Some environments will be fully air-gapped for offline inference near device fleets.

Redwood items / ask list:
1) We will kick off a short vendor questionnaire focused on network controls and crypto (I attached a focused checklist). Please confirm the right SecOps contact for questionnaire follow-ups (Alan?)
2) Can you share a high-level internal network diagram (subnets, NAT/GW, VPN/Direct Connect, any data diode or physical airlock)? A PDF or export is fine.
3) Clarify whether MedGest expects: a) outbound-only NAT egress to a proxy, b) no outbound at all (true air-gap), or c) occasional manual bundle sync to an air-gapped site. This determines offline model cache approach.
4) Any constraints on KMS/HSM usage (customer-managed keys required?) and SOC 2 evidence we should collect now.

Next meeting: propose a 30-min technical follow-up next week to review diagram and pick an isolation pattern (VPC private subnets + egress proxy, mirrored VPC with one-way sync, or fully air-gapped on-prem cache). Rishi and Priyom will join.

Attachments: Redwood netseg checklist (redwood-netseg-checklist-v1.xlsx) — lightweight vendor Q focused on: network boundaries, egress, key management, logging/IDS, and change control.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai
[Attachment: redwood-netseg-checklist-v1.xlsx]

From: Alan Walker <alan.walker@medgest.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Katie Lin <katie@medgest.com>, secops@medgest.com
Date: 2028-07-30T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Network segmentation evaluation & air-gapped deployment options (next steps)

Vanessa —

Thanks for the clear summary and checklist. Confirming: SecOps is the right owner (Alan here). Quick answers to your items below, plus I attached our internal sketch and SOC 2 readiness summary for context.

- SOC 2: readiness assessment complete; control remediation in flight. We expect a Type II report to be issued in Q4 2028. Attached: medgest-soc2-summary-2028Q2.pdf
- Network diagram: attached as medgest-internal-network-diagram.pdf — this is a redacted internal diagram showing segregated subnets for telemetry ingestion, model hosting (on-prem), and admin VPN.
- Isolation modes: Our preferred approach for the POC is a mirrored-onprem model host in a secured data center (option b/c from call): offline model bundles will be uploaded to an air-gapped host via a controlled transfer process (manual sync using signed artifacts).
- KMS/HSM: We require customer-managed keys for any persistent model encryption on on-prem hardware. HSM integration will be part of the procurement for that host.

We’re happy to do the 30-min tech follow-up. How about Tue 2028-08-02 10:00am ET? Also, I'll ask our infra engineer (cc'd: secops@medgest.com) to be present to walk the diagram.

Alan Walker
Senior Director, SecOps | MedGest Health
alan.walker@medgest.com
[Attachments: medgest-internal-network-diagram.pdf; medgest-soc2-summary-2028Q2.pdf]

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Alan Walker <alan.walker@medgest.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-07-30T16:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Network segmentation evaluation & air-gapped deployment options (next steps)

Thanks Alan — appreciated. A few quick clarifying points from our end before Tuesday's call so we can prepare a focused design: 

1) Transfer mechanics: you mentioned manual sync of signed artifacts — can you confirm the file transfer medium (SFTP over private link, physical USB with data-diode transfer, or s3-bucket export with presigned durable manifest)? The technical approach impacts our bundle signing and offline cache strategy.
2) KMS/HSM: we'll draft an HSM integration pattern that supports customer-managed keys (we support PKCS#11 and cloud HSM endpoints) — any preferred vendor (Thales, AWS CloudHSM, Azure Dedicated HSM)?
3) Logging & audit: for the air-gapped hosts, what level of logging will be permitted to leave the environment (audit-only manifests vs full logs)? We want to design a minimal evidence export so you can meet SOC 2 while preserving isolation.

Action: Priyom, can you prepare two design sketches pre-call: (A) VPC with controlled egress + model bundle sync, (B) fully air-gapped on-prem with signed bundles and manual deploy steps. Attach to the calendar invite.

See you Tuesday — thanks Alan & Katie.

Rishi
Head of Solutions Architecture | Redwood Inference

From: Alan Walker <alan.walker@medgest.com>

Cc: Katie Lin <katie@medgest.com>, secops@medgest.com, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-07-31T11:43:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Network segmentation evaluation & air-gapped deployment options (next steps)

Rishi / Vanessa —

Follow-up after a quick internal sync: answers below and one link for the diagram export (we've obfuscated IPs):

- Transfer medium: primary path is SFTP over a private Direct Connect peer. For remote clinic sites where Direct Connect isn't available, we have a physical transfer process (encrypted USB + one-way data diode ingestion).
- Preferred HSM: we are standardizing on Thales HSMs at the data-center level; CloudHSM only where hardware isn't possible.
- Logging: minimal audit manifests (hashes of deployed bundles, deploy timestamps, and operator IDs) can be exported off the air-gapped host. Full system logs will remain behind the data diode.

Link to redacted diagram: https://files.medgest.com/redacted/medgest-network-diagram-v2.pdf

Looking forward to Priyom's sketches. Confirming the Tue 2028-08-02 10:00am ET slot.

Best,
Alan
